problem_description: An incident has been detected in the Online Boutique cluster. Investigate using available tools and identify the root cause and appropriate remediation action.

acceptable_root_causes: native memory stress job causing resource pressure

problem.scenario: an AgentScope native memory stress job creates cluster pressure affecting frontend traffic

telemetry_contract.notes: Requires stress-job metadata plus memory/resource evidence.

problem.notes: Medium native cluster-pressure task; stress-job detector metadata must remain available in raw artifacts.

This suggests either resource pressure on the frontend pods themselves or dependency issues affecting request performance. | Hypotheses: Frontend service is experiencing resource pressure (CPU throttling or memory pressure) that is causing latency symptoms despite having healthy replicas. vs Frontend service is healthy from a resource perspective but experiencing latency due to downstream dependency issues or network problems. | Support: PagerDuty alert specifically mentions "resource-related symptoms" along with latency, suggesting the frontend itself may be under resource pressure. | Uncertainty: I don't know if the latency symptoms are due to resource exhaustion within the frontend service (CPU/memory pressure) or due to dependency latency/failures. The alert mentions both latency and resource-related symptoms but I need metrics to distinguish between these possibilities. | Next evidence: Resource metrics for frontend service to determine if CPU/memory pressure is causing the performance issues, or if the frontend is healthy but experiencing dependency-related latency. | Decision impact: This determines whether the remediation should focus on scaling/resource adjustments for frontend vs investigating and fixing downstream dependencies. | Would change my mind if: If get_metrics shows normal CPU/memory utilization and no throttling or pressure on frontend, I would pivot to investigating dependency latency issues.
